parsed.explanation: No trans-specific criminal statute or traveller-facing restriction is documented; the operative exposures are tier-3: documented societal hostility (concealment, coded networks, 2024), dated but severe violence against trans people (2011, post-coup), and a current state signal — January 2025 rejection of recommendations to combat anti-LGBT violence — indicating thin official recourse and tacit endorsement of impunity. The unequal age of consent (21, 5-10 year penalty) is a sexuality-law lever, secondary, but active for any visitor whose partner or counterparty is under 21; a parent travelling with their own minor faces no documented trans-specific exposure from it. Data-protection statutes marginally reduce outing by institutions. Thin data on borders, facilities, custody and care resolves toward the structural picture: no criminalisation, but hostility with weak recourse — mid-scale, Elevated Risk.

entry_documents.exposure: Not documented. Border, visa, marker and screening practices are unsourced; no claim either way.
entry_documents.interaction: Unknown border treatment of marker mismatch is an open question, not an exposure.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Not documented for trans visitors. The 2020 statutory-rape arrest shows the unequal consent law is enforced against women in same-sex relationships (5-10 year band).
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A visitor with an under-21 partner could enter this criminal pathway; custody conditions unknown.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Not documented. No facility, bathroom, ward or shelter rules sourced.

care_services.exposure: Not documented for visitors; no trans-specific care rules sourced.
care_services.protection: HIV Act 2005-040 mandates targeted protections for vulnerable groups including MSM and mobile populations; privacy statutes (2014-038 Art.18, 2017-045) bar processing of sexual-life data — institutional climate signals.
care_services.interaction: HIV-framed health policy may indirectly support a trans visitor's service access.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Government cancelled an LGBTQ event for 'incitement to debauchery' (2021) and in January 2025 rejected recommendations against anti-LGBT violence and hate speech — official tolerance of impunity (tier 2-3). Religious leaders offered conversion therapy to the 19-year-old in the 2020 case.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: None documented; local organisations protest but state refuses.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: State indifference lowers the cost to hostile actors of targeting an outed visitor.

minors_guardians.exposure: Unequal age of consent (21) with indecent-assault penalty applies if any romantic involvement with an under-21 person; a parent travelling with their own minor faces no documented additional trans-specific exposure.
minors_guardians.interaction: Mother-initiated complaint in 2020 shows family members can trigger prosecution.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: 2011 (post-coup): transgender sex workers frequent targets of verbal abuse, stone throwing and murder; attitudes 'tacit acceptance to violent rejection'. Dated, and sex-worker-specific; no later instance documented and no denominator.
street_violence_police_response.protection: None documented; state rejected anti-violence recommendations in 2025.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Thin recourse: violence findings without documented enforcement response.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Legal-recognition regime, case law outcomes, Article 39 application all undocumented; no documented working remedy for anti-trans harm.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Data-protection statutes limit institutional disclosure; refugee-resource notes protection machinery and case law exist beyond this record (unverified here).
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Thin-data jurisdiction: unresolved questions resolve toward structural hostility, not midpoint.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar tier: administrative/humiliating exposure without criminal custody, remedies slow. Here no border exposure is documented at all, but state impunity signals (2025 rejections) are worse than 0.55-B's functioning appeal desk; roughly comparable overall.

Lower exposure than 0.35-C: no universal reporting/registration machinery, no enforcement regime reaching every visitor, and privacy statutes exist. The hostile climate and impunity signal keep this well above the 0.35 band.

Below 0.75-C: that anchor has documented working remedies (tribunal, compensation, trained officers). Here the state actively rejected anti-violence recommendations and no functioning recourse is documented, so the score sits a full band lower.

parsed.synthesis: The combined operative regime shows no trans-specific criminalisation or traveller-facing restriction, but layers three negatives: documented societal hostility forcing concealment (2024), dated severe violence against trans people (2011, sex-worker-specific, post-coup, no later data), and a current state posture refusing anti-violence commitments (2025). The unequal age of consent is a secondary but active lever for any visitor with an under-21 partner; a guardian with their own minor is not additionally exposed. Privacy statutes are weak institutional climate positives. Worst documented feature is tier 3 — societal hostility with thin recourse — placing this moderately above organised-targeting jurisdictions and clearly below acceptance-with-remedies ones. Rating 0.50; uncertainty is substantial on borders, custody and care.
